Compostable vs Recyclable Flexible Packaging: A Realistic Buyer Comparison

Published August 26, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

Certified compostable films suit brands with collection and industrial composting channels; recyclable polyethylene pouches suit store-drop-off programs. Confirm certification validity, real disposal infrastructure in your market, barrier performance and cost before choosing. Sustainability claims must match how the pack is actually disposed of.

Certification is the starting point

Compostability claims need valid certification (for example, industrial compostability standards) and the label artwork must match the certificate. Confirm the certificate, scope and validity before printing claims.

Disposal infrastructure decides the claim

A compostable pouch that ends up in landfill or a recyclable pouch without a drop-off program performs no better than conventional film. Research your markets real collection channels and design claims accordingly.

Barrier trade-offs are real

Many compostable films offer lower barrier than foil structures, shortening shelf life for sensitive products. Confirm measured barrier values against your product and distribution.

Cost and supply

Sustainable structures often cost more and have different lead times. Compare total cost including claims, testing and certification maintenance at your quantity.

Buyer checklist

  1. Verify certification validity
  2. Check real disposal channels
  3. Compare barrier performance
  4. Cost the full picture
  5. Match claims to reality

Frequently asked questions

Is compostable packaging better for the environment?

Only if the pack reaches a working composting channel; otherwise it may perform no better than conventional film.

Can recyclable pouches be fully recycled?

Most need store drop-off programs and clean, single-material structures; confirm local programs.

Do sustainable films protect food as well?

Often not equally; confirm barrier values against your shelf-life target.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Compostable and recyclable pouches have different specs and different barrier ceilings. Compostable stand-up pouches use bio-based films such as NK 20µm / NKME 20µm / PBS 40µm or Kraft 50gsm / NKME 20µm / PLA 40µm, with TUV AUSTRIA Home Compostable certification and EN 13432 / ASTM D6400 compliance; barrier is OTR ≤ 5.0 cc/m²·day and WVTR ≤ 5.0 g/m²·day. Seal strength is ≥ 25 N / 15 mm and the zipper is compostable PE or PLA at 6–8 mm. Capacity runs 100g–1kg with stand-up, flat-bottom or box-pouch styles.

Frequently Asked Questions

What certifications do compostable pouches carry?

TUV AUSTRIA Home Compostable, with EN 13432 / ASTM D6400 compliance for the certified structures.

How do compostable barriers compare to foil?

Compostable films target OTR ≤ 5.0 cc/m²·day and WVTR ≤ 5.0 g/m²·day — adequate for many dry goods but lower than foil.
